overview: SBA Communications is a real estate investment trust (REIT) and one of the largest independent owners and operators of wireless communications infrastructure in the Americas and Africa, with 46,328 towers as of December 31, 2025 and an average of 1.8 tenants per site. Its core business is leasing space on towers, rooftops and other structures to wireless carriers and other tenants under long-term contracts with built-in rent escalators. SBA operates domestically (roughly 17,500 U.S. towers) and internationally across Central America, Brazil, South Africa, and other Latin American/African markets, having exited smaller, subscale markets (Philippines, Colombia, Argentina, Canada) in 2025 while growing in Central America via a major Millicom tower acquisition.

business_model.summary: SBA generates the vast majority of profit from site leasing — renting space on owned or managed tower structures to wireless carriers under multi-year master lease agreements with contractual rent escalators (often tied to CPI or fixed ~3-4%) and renewal options; site leasing contributed roughly 97.9% of total segment operating profit in FY2025. A smaller, more volatile site development segment provides construction, installation and consulting services to carriers, largely correlated with carrier capex cycles.

revenue_streams.name: Domestic site leasing
revenue_streams.trend: stable, modest growth offset by Sprint/T-Mobile and EchoStar churn

revenue_streams.name: International site leasing
revenue_streams.trend: growing strongly, boosted by Millicom/Central America acquisition and Brazil densification

revenue_streams.name: Site development
revenue_streams.trend: volatile, tied to carrier capex/network deployment activity

business_model.customer_type: B2B — major wireless carriers (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Millicom/Tigo, Vivo, Claro, and other regional operators) under long-term, non-cancelable master lease agreements
business_model.geographic_mix: United States/territories ~66-68% of site leasing revenue; international (Brazil, Central America — Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica — South Africa, Tanzania, Chile, Peru) ~32-33% and rising following 2025 Central America expansion

competitive_position.market_position: Third-largest U.S. publicly-traded tower REIT behind American Tower and roughly comparable in market cap to Crown Castle; the 'Big Three' (AMT, CCI, SBAC) collectively control roughly 70% of privately-owned U.S. tower sites. SBA is now the largest tower operator in Central America following the Millicom transaction.

moat_factors.factor: High switching costs / irreplaceable real estate
moat_factors.description: Towers are difficult and costly to relocate once a carrier's network is built around a site; zoning/permitting barriers make new tower construction slow and costly, locking in incumbent landlords
Master lease agreements typically run 5-10+ years with multiple renewal options and embedded annual rent escalators, providing highly visible, recurring cash flow
Adding a second or third tenant to an existing tower carries minimal incremental cost, driving significant operating leverage as 5G densification adds tenants/equipment per site
Local zoning and environmental approvals make greenfield tower construction difficult, protecting incumbents' site locations
Scale supports lower cost of capital for acquisitions versus smaller private operators, though SBA is smaller and more leveraged than AMT

weaknesses: High customer concentration: top three U.S. carriers (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon) represented roughly 66.5% of 2025 revenue, with T-Mobile alone near 35%

No fiber/data-center diversification comparable to Crown Castle's historical fiber strategy, leaving SBA more purely levered to tower leasing cycles (though exploring 'SBA Edge' modular edge-compute sites)
Smaller scale than American Tower limits negotiating leverage and diversification benefits
Elevated leverage (~6x net debt/EBITDA) relative to some REIT peers, with meaningful floating-rate debt exposure
International footprint concentrated in emerging markets (Brazil, Central America, South Africa) with currency volatility and political/regulatory risk

growth_drivers: 5G network densification in the U.S. — carriers adding mid-band (C-Band) spectrum and additional antennas/radios to existing towers, driving amendment revenue and multi-tenant co-location (~4-5% average organic domestic leasing growth)

Central America expansion via the ~7,000-tower, ~$975 million Millicom sale-leaseback transaction (closed mid/late-2025), making SBA the largest tower operator in the region, plus a build-to-suit pipeline of up to 2,500 additional sites for Millicom
Brazil growth — densification, spectrum auctions, and a historically strong local currency supporting dollar-equivalent lease economics
Portfolio rationalization — exiting subscale, lower-return international markets (Philippines, Colombia, Argentina, Canada in 2025) to concentrate capital in higher-growth, higher-scale markets
New tower builds (build-to-suit) domestically and internationally (~600 planned U.S. builds in 2026) funded by carrier-backed commitments

Emerging edge-computing/data-center land monetization ('SBA Edge') repurposing tower-base land for localized compute modules, targeting AI/low-latency workloads as an early-stage diversification option
Capital returns — resumption of share buybacks in H2 2026 and a 13% dividend increase, supported by AFFO payout ratio of only ~41%, leaving capacity for further increases or portfolio growth

business.description: Prior T-Mobile/Sprint consolidation drives an estimated ~$56 million of cash site leasing revenue churn in 2026 from non-renewed overlapping Sprint leases; further carrier M&A could create similar overlap risk
Top three U.S. carriers account for ~66.5% of revenue; loss, financial distress, or reduced capex from any one is a material risk

EchoStar defaulted on payment obligations in December 2025 after discontinuing its network business; SBA has filed suit and expects limited (but non-zero) impact versus peers given lower relative DISH exposure
Site development revenue and new-lease demand are directly tied to carrier network investment cycles, which can slow between major spectrum/technology upgrade waves

financial.description: Net debt of roughly $12 billion at approximately 6x EBITDA is high for a REIT, limiting financial flexibility
Variable-rate debt is roughly 21% of total indebtedness; rising or persistently elevated rates increase interest expense and refinancing costs on upcoming maturities

Revenue and expenses in Brazil, Chile, Peru, South Africa, Tanzania and Central America are earned/paid in local currency; BRL, local Central American currencies, and ZAR volatility affects reported USD results

regulatory.description: Local and national regulatory changes affecting tower siting, environmental review, or historic preservation could slow new builds or amendments
Must continue to satisfy IRS REIT distribution and asset/income tests to retain favorable tax treatment
Operations in Brazil, Central America and South Africa expose SBA to local telecom regulation, tax, and political instability risk

macro.description: As a highly leveraged REIT, SBA's equity value and refinancing costs are sensitive to the level and direction of interest rates; higher-for-longer rates pressure AFFO and valuation multiples
Brazilian real, South African rand, and Central American currencies can swing meaningfully against the U.S. dollar, affecting translated international revenue and EBITDA
If carriers slow densification spend after initial 5G rollout waves, co-location and amendment revenue growth could decelerate

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. tower industry growth has moderated from the initial 4G/5G buildout surge to a steadier, mid-single-digit organic growth phase driven by densification (more antennas/tenants per tower) rather than net-new tower construction; international markets, especially Latin America, offer higher structural growth from lower initial tenancy ratios and ongoing network rollouts.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — site leasing revenue is highly recurring and contractual (low cyclicality), but site development revenue and new tower construction activity are tied to carrier capital spending cycles, which can be cyclical and lumpy around major spectrum auctions or technology transitions (4G to 5G, and eventually 6G).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — REIT business model relies on continuous access to debt and equity capital markets for acquisitions and refinancing; elevated leverage (~6x net debt/EBITDA) and meaningful floating-rate debt make SBA's cost of capital and AFFO sensitive to rate levels.
key_input_costs: Foreign currency translation (BRL, ZAR, Central American currencies)

recent_developments.event: Sold all towers and exited operations in the Philippines and Colombia, part of a strategy to exit subscale international markets

Closed the approximately 7,000-tower, ~$975 million sale-leaseback acquisition from Millicom in Central America (Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, El Salvador, Nicaragua), making SBA the largest tower operator in the region, with up to 2,500 additional build-to-suit sites committed
Agreed to sell its Canadian tower business (369 towers) to CVC DIF; sale of 365 towers for CA$446 million closed October 2025

EchoStar/DISH defaulted on payment obligations after discontinuing its network business; SBA expects roughly $56 million of cash site leasing revenue churn in 2026 and has filed suit to recover amounts owed
Raised full-year 2026 outlook on strong leasing results; outlined plans for roughly 600 new U.S. tower builds in 2026 and signaled intent to resume share buybacks in H2 2026

Reported total revenue of $715.3 million (+2.3% YoY), AFFO per share of $3.05 (down 3.8% YoY), raised quarterly dividend 13% to $1.25/share, and modestly increased full-year 2026 site leasing revenue, FFO, and AFFO guidance; repurchased over 916,000 shares for $175 million at an average price of $191.00
Sell-side price target cuts from several brokers (RBC, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, BMO) in October 2026, reflecting lower growth expectations even as consensus rating remains Buy/Outperform

items.notes: Modest increase vs. prior 2026 guidance, driven by higher straight-line revenue and FX
Benefiting from improved net cash interest expense outlook
Modest increase versus prior full-year guidance
Improved interest expense outlook cited as a driver of the overall guidance raise
Reflects ~4-5% organic growth offset by Sprint/EchoStar churn
Boosted by full-year contribution from Millicom Central America acquisition and Brazil strength
U.S. build-to-suit program; additional international builds under Millicom build-to-suit commitment (up to 2,500 sites)

items.target: Dividend $1.25/share quarterly (13% YoY increase); buybacks to resume
items.notes: Dividend represents ~41% of AFFO, leaving capacity for further increases or buybacks; management called current valuation a low-risk, high-return repurchase opportunity

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasized confidence in domestic 5G densification trends (mid-band spectrum deployment favoring tower-heavy builds), continued strength in Brazil supported by currency and spectrum auctions, and successful integration of the Millicom Central America portfolio. Management described portfolio exits from subscale markets (Philippines, Colombia, Argentina, Canada) as capital discipline to concentrate on higher-return core markets. On the EchoStar default, management said impact to date has not been material and litigation is underway to recover amounts owed. Capital allocation priority remains: accretive acquisitions/builds, then buybacks, then dividend growth, with debt paydown considered in a high-rate environment.

bull_case: Highly recurring, contractually escalating site leasing revenue (97.9% of segment operating profit) provides defensive, inflation-linked cash flow with minimal churn outside known carrier-consolidation events
5G mid-band densification in the U.S. continues to drive high-margin co-location and amendment revenue with minimal incremental capex, supporting operating leverage
Central America expansion (Millicom deal) and Brazil growth give SBA a large, high-growth international runway with lower tower tenancy ratios than the mature U.S. market
Disciplined portfolio rationalization (exiting Philippines, Colombia, Argentina, Canada) focuses capital on higher-return core markets and should improve consolidated margins over time
Shareholder capital returns resuming — 13% dividend increase and planned H2 2026 buyback resumption — with AFFO payout ratio of only ~41% leaving room for further increases
bear_case: High leverage (~6x net debt/EBITDA) and ~21% floating-rate debt make SBA more sensitive to a higher-for-longer interest rate environment than less-levered peers
Customer concentration risk remains acute — top three U.S. carriers are ~66.5% of revenue, and further carrier consolidation or financial distress (as with EchoStar/DISH) could drive meaningful churn
EchoStar/DISH default and related litigation create an industry-wide overhang on tower REIT revenue visibility, even if SBA's direct exposure is smaller than peers
Emerging-market currency exposure (BRL, ZAR, Central American currencies) introduces earnings volatility that is difficult to hedge fully and can swing reported international results

Smaller scale than American Tower and recent multiple compression (declining sell-side price targets in October 2026) suggest the market is discounting slower growth or execution risk in the post-divestiture portfolio
